summary.tldr: Sets a six-month minimum jail term for perjury before Parliament and lets a House of Parliament fine people for contempt.
what_it_does: Sets a minimum punishment of six months in prison for perjury before a House of Parliament or one of its committees, while keeping the maximum at 14 years.
Allows the Senate or the House of Commons to order a fine of up to $50,000 for conduct that the House finds to be contempt of Parliament.
Makes a contempt fine enforceable in Federal Court once a certified copy of the order is filed there.
Provides that recovery of the fine is not affected by prorogation or dissolution of Parliament.
States that evidence under section 12 of the Parliament of Canada Act is admissible against the witness in proceedings under that section.
who_it_affects: People found in contempt of Parliament
The Senate and House of Commons
summary.background: Section 132 of the Criminal Code already makes perjury an indictable offence. The bill also adds a new fine process to the Parliament of Canada Act.
